claims.statement: The backend money model uses two representations: raw numeric values (market prices, position `quantity` and `average_cost`) are `Decimal` in the API types, while any currency-tagged amount is `stockholm.Money`; `Account.currency` and `Security.currency` are `stockholm.currency.Currency` while `Position.currency` is a plain `str | None`, and the read schemas downgrade every currency field to `str` (`HoldingRead.currency`/`security_currency`/`display_currency`, `AccountHoldingsRead.currency`, `AccountHoldingRead.currency`/`display_currency`) with `AccountSchema` using an explicit `@field_serializer("currency")` to emit its `Currency` as a code string, so `Currency` survives only in the service layer and the write path.

A `stockholm.Money` serializes to JSON as a single currency-suffixed string field (for example `{"value": "500.00 USD"}`), not as structured `units`/`nanos`/`currencyCode`; tests assert `payload["totals"]["cost"]["value"] == "500.00 USD"` and that `result["cost"]["value"]` ends with `" CAD"`.

Currency conversion is centralized in `PositionService._currency_convert`, which returns the value untouched when the source and target currency codes match exactly and otherwise calls `self._fx_rates.convert(...)`, rounds to 2 decimal places, and re-wraps the result as `Money`; the service receives that converter through its `fx_rates` constructor argument, and `position_service_factory` supplies it by resolving `FxRateProvider` from the container and awaiting `fx_provider.converter()`.

Conversion is applied per position before accumulation rather than to stored values: `_calculate_holdings` converts each position's value and cost into the account currency as it walks the positions and accumulates account-currency `total_value`/`total_cost`, deriving `total_cost` as `value_money - pl_money` from the already-converted pair, so positions never have their `average_cost` or `currency` rewritten by FX. `_calculate_holding` adds a second, display-facing hop by converting the account-currency value again into `display_currency` (default: the account currency).

`HoldingRead` reports the same logical amount several times — `unconverted_total_value` and `unconverted_profit_loss` in `security_currency`, `total_value`/`profit_loss`/`converted_average_cost`/`converted_latest_price` in the account `currency`, and `display_total_value` in `display_currency` — where `security_currency` is actually `position.currency or security.currency`, so a position-level currency overrides the security's throughout the cost and value math while `latest_price` and `average_cost` are copied verbatim (latest_price straight from the stored price); the account-scoped holdings table renders the converted line only when `holding.security_currency !== holding.currency`.

`get_total_for_account` re-converts the account-currency positions totals into the requested currency and returns the full `AccountTotals` (`cost`, `value`, `cash`, `net_deposits`, `profit_loss`, `return_percent`, `basis`, `unpriced_positions`, `pricing_incomplete`) computed by `_account_performance`, where `cost` is the per-position converted `quantity × average_cost` plus converted `free_cash` and `value` is the per-position converted `quantity × latest close` plus the same cash; the type is served by `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` (optional `?currency=` restricted to the supported display currencies, else 422) and pushed as `AccountTotalsUpdatedMessage` by the `recalculate_all_account_totals_task` Huey task, but the frontend never handles `account_totals_updated` — it still fetches totals over HTTP and caches them per account.

`_account_performance` chooses the P/L basis: when `account.net_deposits` is not `None` the basis is `net_deposits` and `profit_loss = value - net_deposits` (total value including cash minus deposits), with `return_percent = profit_loss / net_deposits * 100` reported only when `net_deposits != 0`; otherwise the basis is `cost` and `profit_loss = positions_value - positions_cost` with cash excluded from both numerator and denominator, and `return_percent` is `None` when the positions cost is zero. `AccountHoldingsRead` projects those onto `total_profit_loss`, `total_profit_loss_percent` and `profit_loss_basis`, and the free-cash asset test asserts `total_value == 1500`, `total_profit_loss == 500` and `total_profit_loss_percent == 50.0` for `1500 - 1000`.

The frontend `Money` interface is `{ value?: string; units?: number; nanos?: number; currencyCode?: string }`, and `moneyToNumber` prefers `units + nanos / 1e9` when `units` is a number, otherwise falls back to `parseFloat(value)`, returning `0` for null, undefined, or unparseable input; `money(m)` renders `$<localized number>`.

Because the API emits `value` strings like `"500.00 CAD"` with no `units`, the `units`/`nanos` branch of `moneyToNumber` is unused against the live backend and real responses succeed only because `parseFloat` stops at the first non-numeric character; frontend test fixtures supply `units`/`nanos` alongside `value`, so the units path only looks alive in tests, and a serializer or parser change on either side must update both the backend shape and the frontend `Money` type together or amounts silently become wrong or `0`.

`blendedAverageCost` computes the quantity-weighted mean of `average_cost` across holdings, returning `0` for an empty list, zero total quantity, or all-missing costs, and treating a missing `average_cost` as `0` so an unknown-cost holding pulls the blended figure toward zero rather than being excluded.

Holdings period math runs on JS `number`: `getBenchmarkPrice` returns the average cost for `period === 'ALL'` and otherwise the close of the most recent candle at or before the period cutoff (falling back to the earliest candle), and `calculateHoldingGain` returns `gainAmount = (currentPrice - benchmarkPrice) * quantity` and `gainPercent = priceDiff / benchmarkPrice * 100` guarded to `0` when the benchmark is `0`.

Precision is lost at defined storage boundaries: `PositionModel.quantity` is `DECIMAL(16, 8)` but `PositionModel.average_cost` is `Float` and `PositionModel.currency` a nullable `String(3)`, `AccountModel.currency` is a plain `String` (while the service-layer API type is `Currency`), and `AccountModel.net_deposits` and `AccountModel.free_cash` are `Float`, so cash-flow P&L and the cash contribution to both totals inherit float error.

`src/account/csv/parser.py` parses quantities and book values as `Decimal` after stripping `,` and `$`, and computes `average_cost` as `(book_value / quantity).quantize(Decimal("0.0001"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)`, returning `None` for non-positive quantity or missing book value.

`get_holdings_by_security` values each row as `float(quantity) × float(latest close)` from `MarketPricesApi.get_latest_close`, wraps it as `Money(round(value, 2), security.currency)`, converts it into the account currency, and divides by `get_total_for_account(account_id, account.currency).value.amount` to produce `account_percentage` (only when that denominator is positive); `total_value` stays in the security's currency, `display_total_value` is converted into the request's display currency (defaulting to the account's), and `account_total_value` is the same cash-inclusive account total used as the denominator.

CSV import currency selection feeds every downstream aggregate: `chosen_currency` is the trimmed, upper-cased per-account value from the import request, else the currency the parser derived for that account (which falls back to `CAD` when no `currency`, `book_value_currency_market` or `market_price_currency` value is present), else `CAD`; an existing account's currency is updated when it differs from `chosen_currency`, and new accounts are created with `currency=Currency(chosen_currency)`. The parser additionally assigns each position its own currency from `currency` → `book_value_currency_market` → `book_value_currency_cad` → the account currency.

`tests/routers/test_accounts.py` pins the totals endpoint's money contract: `test_account_totals_success` asserts the `cost`, `value`, `cash` and `profit_loss` string values end with ` CAD` plus `basis == "cost"`, `test_account_totals_converts_to_requested_currency` asserts `?currency=USD` switches every suffix to ` USD`, `test_account_totals_unsupported_currency_returns_422` rejects `XYZ` with 422, and the not-found/not-owned tests assert 404.

Because the FX conversion target is the account's own `currency` for every stored aggregate, changing an account's currency re-bases every converted total, value and P&L for that account without modifying any stored position — CSV import is one path that does this, updating an existing account's currency when a different `chosen_currency` is supplied — while `get_user_holdings` and `get_holdings_by_security` add a second conversion into the user's `display_currency` preference for the `display_*` fields only.

`account.free_cash`, wrapped as `Money(free_cash, account.currency)` and converted into the target currency, is added to both `AccountTotals.cost` and `AccountTotals.value` (and reported separately as `cash`) inside `_account_performance`, which both `get_total_for_account` and `get_account_holdings` call — so cash sits in the reported totals, `AccountTotals.cost` stops being a pure cost basis once cash is non-zero, and the `cost`-basis `profit_loss` deliberately excludes it. Every consumer of `AccountTotals.value`, including `get_holdings_by_security`'s `account_percentage` denominator, is therefore measuring cash plus holdings.

Per-position products are rounded to 2 decimal places before conversion or accumulation: `_calculate_holding` rounds `current_price_money × quantity` and `quantity × average_cost` into `unconverted_total_value`/`unconverted_cost`, `get_holdings_by_security` rounds `quantity × latest close` before converting, and `_currency_convert` rounds every converted amount (so a security → account → display chain rounds twice, leaving up to ~0.005 of drift per position and hop) — making each aggregate a sum of rounded per-position values rather than the rounded sum of exact values, and CSV-imported `average_cost` is itself quantized to 4 decimals.

Missing prices and missing FX rates fail differently. A position whose security raises `SecurityNotFoundError` is logged, counted and skipped, and a position with no stored price still gets a row (`total_value = 0.0`, `profit_loss = None`, `latest_price = None`, `converted_latest_price = None`, with `converted_average_cost` still converted) while contributing nothing to `value`, `cost` or P/L; both totals paths report the count as `unpriced_positions` and flag `pricing_incomplete`, and `get_holdings_by_security` returns an empty list with `total == 0` when the security lookup fails. A missing FX rate is not handled at all: `_currency_convert` has no fallback and lets the `currencyconverter` error propagate, so `GET /accounts/{account_id}/totals` fails the request while `_recalculate_all_account_totals` catches per account, logs, and continues.

`total-profit-loss-buttons.svelte` is the live renderer for account totals on the account list, the account detail page and the `/holdings` header: it converts its `Money | number` props with `moneyToNumber`, accepts `profitLoss`, `returnPercent` and `basisLabel` props, derives the return percentage as `(profitLoss / cost) * 100` when it is omitted, falls back to `Money.currencyCode` for the display currency, and formats with `Intl.NumberFormat('en-CA', { style: 'currency', currency })`; the account list drives it from the totals endpoint with `costBasis = basis === 'net_deposits' ? net_deposits : cost` and `currency = account.currency`. The `money()` helper in `money.ts` renders a bare `$` with no currency code and no fixed decimals and has no production caller (only `money.test.ts` imports it), while the holdings views use the same explicit-currency `Intl.NumberFormat` helper because they mix security and account currencies.

The holdings sidebar normalizes currencies before dividing: `holding-group.svelte` requests every account's totals in the user's `display_currency` preference (default `CAD`) and sums them for `totalPortfolioValue`, and its numerator is the sum of the rows' `display_total_value`, so the `% of Portfolio` ratio is single-currency (the tests cover the cross-currency case explicitly). The mixed-currency sum that remains is the `holdings-modal.svelte` footer `Total` row, which sums each holding's account-currency `total_value` and formats the sum with the first holding's currency.

Market price columns are fixed-point: `PriceModel` and `IntradayPriceModel` store `open`, `high`, `low`, `close` (and `adjusted_close` on `PriceModel`) as `DECIMAL(16, 8)`, and user-entered price fields share that convention — `PriceAlertModel.target_price` and `SecurityValuationModel`/`SecurityValuationHistoryModel` `lower_bound`/`upper_bound` are also `DECIMAL(16, 8)` — while their write schemas (`PriceAlertWrite.target_price`, `SecurityValuationWrite.lower_bound`/`upper_bound`) accept an unconstrained `Decimal` and the frontend `ValuationClient` types both valuation bounds as plain `number`, so 8 fractional digits is the effective precision and the database, not validation, rounds anything more precise.

`holdings-metrics.ts` also owns the holdings-table ratio helpers: `calculatePercentOfTotal` and `calculatePercentOfAccount` both return `0` for non-finite inputs or a non-positive denominator, and `formatHoldingPercent` renders one decimal place or `-` for null/non-finite values, so these ratios are always plain JS `number` derived from float-typed `HoldingRead` fields.

`blendedAverageCost` has three production consumers, not one: `holding-group.svelte` (the "Average" row, formatted `en-US`), the `holdings-modal.svelte` footer `portfolioAvgPrice`, and the security detail page's `averageBuyingPrice`, which feeds the chart's average-price overlay line via `security-chart.svelte`'s `averagePrice` prop.

The cross-account holdings page never sums across currencies: `frontend/src/routes/holdings/+page.svelte` builds `currencyTotals` with `aggregateAccountTotals` from each visible account's server totals tagged with `account.currency`, which yields one bucket per currency, uses `sum(profit_loss) / sum(net_deposits)` only when every account in the bucket reports the `net_deposits` basis, and otherwise falls back to `sum(profit_loss) / sum(value - profit_loss)` labelled `mixed basis` with no basis amount — the pattern any new cross-account aggregate should copy; `portfolio-list-item.svelte` reuses the same aggregator.

The watchlist surfaces deliberately render no currency symbol: `watchlist-utils.ts` exposes `formatPrice` (2 decimals, `-` for absent or unparseable) and `formatPriceChangePercent` (signed 2 decimals, `0.00%` for zero and negative zero), and `watchlists/+page.svelte` renders `SecuritySchema.current_price` and `daily_price_change_percent` through them; the module also carries its own object-shaped `formatValuationRange` accepting `number | string` bounds, separate from the `$lib/utils/finance/valuation` variant the holdings table uses.

Only the cross-account holdings table owns the valuation-range column: `frontend/src/lib/components/holdings/holdings-table.svelte` formats `row.valuation_lower`/`valuation_upper` with `formatValuationRange` from `$lib/utils/finance/valuation`, whereas the account-scoped `frontend/src/lib/components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte` has no valuation column at all — so the range-formatting contract lives on the cross-account surface.

`total-profit-loss-buttons.svelte` falls back to a signed `$x.xx` string when `Intl.NumberFormat` rejects the currency code, and although its `effectiveCurrency` derivation contains a `Money.currencyCode` fallback, the `currency` prop defaults to `'CAD'`, so the display currency is in practice whichever currency the caller passes (the account list passes `account.currency`).

`moneyToNumber` reads only `units`/`nanos` or the `value` string and ignores `currencyCode`, so the parsed number never carries a currency and every call site must pass the currency separately to its formatter; it has four production importers — `accounts-list-item.svelte`, `total-profit-loss-buttons.svelte`, `holding-group.svelte` and `frontend/src/lib/utils/finance/account-totals.ts` — and the `Money` type additionally backs `AccountTotals` and `Holding` in `frontend/src/lib/types/account.ts`.

`src/market/currency.py` owns listing-currency resolution: `normalize_currency` returns `None` for blank input, folds provider pence (`GBp`, `gbx`) to `GBX` and upper-cases everything else, and `resolve_listing_currency` prefers the normalized company-profile currency, falling back to the deterministic `EXCHANGE_DEFAULT_CURRENCY` table (`TSX → CAD`, `LSE → GBX`, `NYSE`/`NASDAQ`/`NYSEARCA`/`AMEX`/`None` → `USD`); a `MarketDataNotFoundError` caches the fallback while provider/configuration errors return it uncached with a warning, and the resolved code is cached through `EndpointResponseCache` under `data_class="metrics"`, `endpoint="listing_currency"`.

`GBX` is a pence unit with no bridge to `GBP` anywhere in the repository: LSE listings and provider pence both resolve to `GBX`, the FX layer is ECB-based and quotes `GBP` (the FX test fixture's ECB header row is `Date,USD,GBP`), no non-test code maps `GBX` to `GBP`, `GBX` never appears in `frontend/src`, and `_currency_convert` only short-circuits on an exact code match — so converting a GBX amount, or rendering it through `Intl.NumberFormat`, is unverified territory that a change must handle deliberately.

`src/market/fx.py` supplies the converter `PositionService` uses: `refresh_fx_rates` downloads `currency_converter.ECB_URL`, rejects a payload that is not a readable zip, and stores the base64 zip plus today's fetch date atomically under `fx:ecb:zip`/`fx:ecb:fetched_at` (driven by the `daily_fx_refresh` Huey periodic task), while `FxRateProvider.converter()` builds a `CurrencyConverter` from that zip at most once per fetch date and caches it at module level (bounded to four entries, a corrupt zip negatively cached per fetch date), falling back to the bundled snapshot whenever Redis is empty/unreachable or the zip is unreadable and logging a warning when the freshest rate is more than 3 business days old.

A second, user-facing conversion hop is driven by the stored `display_currency` preference (`UserApi.get_display_currency` defaults to `CAD`; `SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_CURRENCIES` is `CAD`/`USD`/`EUR`/`GBP`): `HoldingRead` carries `display_total_value` + `display_currency` produced by converting the account-currency value again, `GET /accounts/holdings` and `GET /accounts/holdings/{security_id}` pass that preference into `get_user_holdings`/`get_holdings_by_security`, and `UserHoldingRead` adds the owning account to a `HoldingRead` so cross-account surfaces can sum `display_total_value` without mixing currencies.
